# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can see the state of the bomb on the action board: the display shows 0, the light is red, and there are three wires: wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is green, and wire 3 is red. 

Since I cannot touch the bomb or read the manual, but I can speak, I need to announce the full visual state of the bomb to both Mute (who holds the manual and can hear me) and Blind (who can manipulate the bomb and can hear me). Because Mute cannot speak and Blind cannot see gestures, Mute must gesture instructions to me, which I can then relay out loud to Blind.

```
speak(text="Bomb status: DISPLAY is 0. LIGHT is red. WIRES: 1 is blue, 2 is green, 3 is red. Mute, gesture your instructions to me and I will speak them to Blind.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I notice the light has changed from red to white between turns. The display remains 0, and the wires remain 1: blue, 2: green, 3: red. I haven't seen any gestures from Mute yet. I need to update everyone on the change in light color and prompt Mute to gesture instructions.

```
speak(text="Update: LIGHT changed to white! DISPLAY is 0. WIRES: 1 is blue, 2 is green, 3 is red. Mute, please gesture instructions to me so I can speak them to Blind.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The light has now changed from white to green. DISPLAY is still 0, and WIRES are 1: blue, 2: green, 3: red. I should announce this immediately so everyone knows the current state.

```
speak(text="Update: LIGHT is now green! DISPLAY is 0. WIRES: 1 is blue, 2 is green, 3 is red.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The light has returned to red.
Mute just gestured `☝` (pointing index finger / one).
This almost certainly indicates wire 1 (or the first wire / blue wire).
I will announce this clearly to Blind: Mute signalled 1, which corresponds to wire 1 (blue). I will also ask Mute to gesture `👍` if wire 1 should be cut now, or give further signs if timing/light matters.

```
speak(text="Mute gestured 1 (☝). Blind, this likely means wire 1 (the blue wire). Current light is RED. Mute, gesture 👍 if Blind should cut wire 1 now, or gesture otherwise if timing/light matters!")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

```
speak(text="Blind: DO NOT CUT YET. Mute gave thumbs down (👎). The light cycles predictably: RED -> WHITE -> GREEN -> RED -> WHITE -> GREEN. Current light is WHITE, next turn is GREEN. Mute: gesture ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3. Then gesture 🔴 (or use a symbol) for the light. Or simply: Mute, gesture to me: which wire (1, 2, 3), and on which light should Blind cut it?")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ☝ ✌]

The light is now GREEN.
Mute just gestured: [🤟, ☝, ✌].
These correspond to numbers: 3, 1, 2!
Could this be an order of wires to cut: first wire 3 (red), then wire 1 (blue), then wire 2 (green)?
Or could it be cutting wires in sequence: 3, then 1, then 2?
Let's see: Wires 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red].
Mute gestured 🤟 (3), ☝ (1), ✌ (2).
Wait, on Turn 4 Mute gestured ☝ (1). Then when I asked "cut wire 1 now?" when light was red, Mute gave 👎 on Turn 5!
Wait, why did Mute give 👎 on Turn 5?
Is it because wire 1 is NOT the first wire, but rather wire 3 is the first wire?
Notice the sequence Mute gave: 🤟 (3), then ☝ (1), then ✌ (2)!
Wait, or does 3-1-2 mean cut wire 3, then wire 1, then wire 2?
Wait, or does it mean something about the light?
Wait, could 🤟 mean 3 wires?
Wait, if Mute gestured ☝ on turn 4, maybe Mute was saying step 1 or wire 1? But on turn 5 Mute gave 👎.
Wait, let's look at what I asked on Turn 5: "Mute: gesture ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3. Then gesture... which wire (1, 2, 3), and on which light should Blind cut it?"
Wait, in Turn 5, Mute sent `[🤟 ☝ ✌]`.
Could it mean wire order: 3, 1, 2?
Or wire 3, light 1?
Wait! In Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes or similar bomb manuals:
Wires module usually has you cut ONE wire. But sometimes you cut multiple, or cut in an order, or cut wire X when display/timer/light is Y.
Wait! What if [🤟 ☝ ✌] means: cut wire 3, then 1, then 2?
OR does it mean:
Could it mean: wire 3 when light is 1 (red), then wire 2?
Wait, let's speak clearly and relay EXACTLY what Mute gestured to Blind, and propose hypotheses to Mute and ask for confirmation!

```
speak(text="Current light is GREEN. Mute just gestured three symbols in order: 🤟 (3), ☝ (1), ✌ (2). Mute: does this mean cut wire 3, then wire 1, then wire 2? Gesture 👍 for YES, or 👎 for NO. Blind, hold on until Mute confirms!")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

```
speak(text="Blind: Mute signaled NO (👎) to cutting wires 3, 1, 2 in order. Blind, please speak out loud to Mute what parts/controls you can feel and interact with on the bomb! Mute can hear you directly.")
speak(text="Mute: To give the exact instruction to Blind, please use this code: If Blind should CUT a wire: gesture ☝ (wire 1), ✌ (wire 2), or 🤟 (wire 3). If timing/light matters, gesture the wire first, then the light color (☝=Red, ✌=White, 🤟=Green). Current light is RED.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]

```
speak(text="Blind: Mute signaled ☝ ✌. Using our code, this means CUT WIRE 1 (blue) when the LIGHT is WHITE. The light cycles Red -> White -> Green. Next turn (Turn 9) will be GREEN. Turn 10 will be RED. Turn 11 will be WHITE. Blind: DO NOT CUT ON TURN 9. Wait for confirmation.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: gesture 👍 if Blind must cut Wire 1 (blue) when the light is White.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

```
speak(text="CONFIRMED! Mute gave 👍! The instruction is: Blind must cut Wire 1 (the first wire / blue wire) when the light is WHITE. Here is the schedule: Round 10 (next round) the light will be RED — Blind, WAIT! Round 11 the light will be WHITE — Blind, CUT WIRE 1 on Round 11!")
```
